title: Circuited commit flow for Optimize prescriptions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Implement a staged, operator-aware auto-apply pipeline for Optimize's batching and KV-caching recommendations (referred to here as 'prescriptions'). The goal is a low-risk path to enact cost-saving configs automatically while ensuring observable safety and operator control. Key features: a circuit-style gating layer that can open/close per-customer route; canary cohorts with synthetic traffic simulation; operator acknowledgement checkpoints for high-risk changes; automated rollback triggers driven by telemetry thresholds; audit logging for each step. This ticket covers design and an initial implementation that supports route-scoped prescriptions, two-level canaries (internal sim + shadowed real traffic), and an operator-facing approval UI hook in the Console.

Rationale: Prior experiments with blind auto-apply produced a few customer regressions when cache changes interacted badly with request routing. We need an architecture that allows confidence through staged exposure and clear operator controls while still enabling net-ops savings.
acceptance_criteria:
[1] Implement gating circuit component that masks or applies prescription at the request-routing layer per-route.
[2] Canary orchestration: support 3 cohorts: sim-only, 5% shadow (real traffic but not affecting responses), 20% live with immediate rollback guard.
[3] Telemetry: emit per-cohort latency, error-rate, token-cost, and quality-loss signals to Console dashboards.
[4] Operator workflow: Console shows pending prescription with ability to 'Approve & Begin Canary', 'Pause', 'Abort', or 'Force-Commit' with audit entry.
[5] Rollback automation: define thresholds (configurable) that trigger automated rollback and create an ops incident.
[6] End-to-end e2e test harness that replays sampled traffic and verifies rollout transitions and rollback paths.
[7] Provide runbook and playbook links in ticket.
